s.how: Wrap 12 grissini breadsticks with half a slice of prosciutto each, from 100g, spiralling it around the top half. Warm 200g mixed olives in a small pan with 2 tbsp olive oil, the zest of 1 orange, 1 crushed garlic clove and a sprig of rosemary for 3 minutes, then cool slightly. Cut 150g vintage cheddar into cubes. Stand the grissini in a tall glass and serve with the olives and cheese.

s.note: Rusty, the best mate with the bad ideas
s.how: Bake 1kg frozen chips at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once, and toss with 2 tsp chicken salt while hot. Melt 30g butter in a small pan, add 1 finely chopped small onion and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour for 1 minute, then whisk in 400ml beef stock and 1 tsp Worcestershire and simmer 5 minutes. Strain into a jug. Serve the chips in a big basket with the gravy for pouring.

m.note: waiting by the phone for the ransom call
m.how: Stretch 750g pizza dough into two 30cm rounds on oiled trays. Mix 100ml pizza sauce with 3 tbsp barbecue sauce and spread over the bases. Scatter with 300g grated mozzarella. Top with 100g pepperoni, 100g chopped ham, 3 rashers chopped bacon and 2 Italian sausages, squeezed from the skins in small pieces. Bake at 240C for 12 to 14 minutes until the crust is golden and the meat is crisp.

w.note: the cookie fortune Miss Crock sits on
w.how: Beat 125g soft butter with 150g brown sugar, add 1 egg, then mix in 220g self-raising flour and 150g chocolate chips. Roll 12 balls, flatten slightly and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until golden at the edges.

d.how: Chill 4 tall glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Blend 600ml cold full cream milk, 8 scoops vanilla ice cream and 6 crushed chocolate chip cookies until thick but still a little chunky. Pour into the glasses, top with whipped cream from 150ml thickened cream and sprinkle with 2 more crushed cookies. Sit a whole cookie on the rim of each glass.
